newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Natwest Markets to acquire Wheelock Natwest.
newsitem.headline: Natwest Markets to acquire Wheelock Natwest.

text.p: National Westminter Bank Plc's unit Natwest Markets said on Tuesday it had agreed to acquire Wheelock and Co Ltd's stake in Hong Kong-based 50-50 joint venture Wheelock Natwest Ltd.
Terms and details of the acquisition were not disclosed.

"Asia is an integral part of Natwest Market's global ambitions and this acquisition demonstrates further our commitment to developing our securities and investment banking operations in the region," said John Howland-Jackson, chairman of Natwest Market's operations in Asia-Pacific.
The Wheelock Natwest joint venture was formed May 1994 and started operating in the second half of 1995. Net assets at December 31, 1995 were HK$488 million.

"A number of changes in the industry and in the overall regulatory environment for securities trading businesses, coupled with an increased focus by Weelock Natwest on such activities, have led the shareholders to conclude that it is in the best interests of the business for it to become a wholly owned subsidiary of the Natwest Group," the companies said in a joint statement.
Natwest Markets and Wheelock confirmed that Wheelock Natwest Investment Management, the fund management arm of Wheelock Natwest, closed on October 31.
The closure followed Natwest Market's acquistion earlier this year of Gartmore Plc, which manages substantial Asian funds from offices in London and Tokyo.
Howland-Jackson, former deputy chief executive of Natwest Markets, will relocate to Hong Kong following his appointment as chairman of Natwest Market's Asia-Pacific operations.
